title: Data assurance playbook for enterprise sellers
body:
Purpose:
This doc is a compact playbook for Sales/SEs to use when discussing Redwood's security posture and compliance readiness (SOC2/ISO/HIPAA), data handling guarantees, and audit-log capabilities. It combines concise customer-facing lines, recommended contract/audit-log language, competitive positioning notes, and an internal checklist for evidence requests.

Audience:
- Enterprise sellers and solution engineers
- AE + Legal pre-sales leads
- Field SEs doing compliance/technical deep-dive calls

High-level positioning (one-liners for pitches):
- Hosted API: "Redwood operates with SOC 2 Type II controls for our hosted inference service and provides per-route token cost & latency tracing—so teams can get predictable, auditable LLM inference with minimal ops work."
- Dedicated: "Reserved capacity with isolated GPU pools; same API surface as hosted, but with stronger isolation and evidence options for audits and BAAs."
- Private (VPC/on-prem): "If your data policy requires full control, our Private deployment is engineered for customer-controlled networking, KMS/HSM integration, and air-gapped options."

What we can say (approved safe claims):
- We maintain a third-party SOC 2 Type II attestation for our hosted environment (controls around availability, change mgmt, access control, and monitoring).
- ISO 27001: we have an implemented ISMS and are in (or maintain) ISO 27001 certification for our control plane. (If certification pending, say: "ISO-aligned ISMS in place; certification in progress.")
- HIPAA: we support HIPAA workloads for Dedicated and Private deployments and can sign a BAA for eligible enterprise contracts.
- Audit logs: we capture request-level audit events (timestamp, request id, model id, model version, tokens consumed, caller id, route metadata) and can provide log exports and retention options for enterprise plans.
- Data handling: customer data in-hosted inference is logically isolated per account; short-lived cache for inference performance; optional customer-managed keys for encryption-at-rest in Dedicated/Private.

What we should avoid (do not claim without confirmation):
- "We store or own customer prompts/responses for training" — default: we do not use customer data for model training unless explicitly contracted.
- "All logs contain PII-free content" — log contents depend on what the application sends; recommend warning customers about not sending PHI over hosted unless under a BAA and configured controls.

Evidence types to offer (what SEs can upload to a prospect portal or send after NDA):
- SOC 2 Type II report (redacted) or SOC 2 letter of attestation
- ISO 27001 certificate (if applicable)
- BAA template and example signed BAAs (with redactions)
- Pen test summary and remediation notes (redacted)
- Audit-log samples (scrubbed) and retention policy doc
- Architecture diagram showing dedicated/private isolation, KMS integration, and network controls

Suggested contract/audit-log clauses (templates to propose to Legal):
- Audit log access clause (customer-friendly): 
  "Provider will retain and make available, upon request and subject to the terms below, audit logs related to Customer’s use of the Service for a retention period of X days. Audit logs will include timestamps, request identifiers, model/version identifiers, and metadata sufficient for Customer to reconstruct request activity. Provider will not disclose request/response payloads without a lawful request or Customer consent."

- Limited audit rights (provider protections): 
  "Customer may exercise audit rights no more than once per 12 months, subject to reasonable notice and execution of a mutual NDA. Audits may be performed remotely or via vendor-provided artifacts (redacted reports, logs). Any on-site audit requires minimum 60 days notice and is subject to Provider’s security procedures."

- BAA language starter (HIPAA): 
  "Provider will enter into a Business Associate Agreement (BAA) for Dedicated or Private deployments where Provider processes Protected Health Information on behalf of Customer. Provider’s administrative, physical, and technical safeguards are documented in the BAA and annual attestations are available upon request."

Audit-log contents (recommended default schema we can offer):
- timestamp (ISO8601)
- request_id (uuid)
- customer_id / tenant_id (pseudonymized id)
- api_route / model_id / model_version
- tokens_in / tokens_out / token_cost
- response_status / error_code
- region / hosting_zone
- caller_ip or caller_region (depending on privacy)
- event_type (create, update, infer, auth)
- actor (service account or user id)
- retention_tag (plan: 90/365/730 days)
Notes: for PHI-sensitive customers, recommend disabling caller_ip and asking customers to use Private deployments with VPC logging centralization.

Sales Q&A (concise answers):
- Q: "Do you sign BAAs?" A: "Yes—BAAs are supported for Dedicated and Private deployments; we generally do not process PHI on hosted plans without a BAA and a vendor review. Talk to Legal/CS for exceptions."
- Q: "Where is data stored and how long?" A: "Data for hosted inference is ephemeral: request data is cached transiently for latency; durable logs and metrics are retained according to plan (e.g., 90/365/730 days). Encryption in transit and at rest is enforced; Dedicated/Private customers can bring keys."
- Q: "Can customers run their own encryption keys?" A: "Yes—Dedicated and Private support customer-managed keys (KMS/HSM integrations)."

Competitive differentiation (talking points):
- vs big cloud managed LLM APIs: Redwood offers consistent API across hosted/dedicated/private plus clearer routing and fallbacks; private deployments + BAAs are first-class rather than a niche.
- vs inference infra vendors (self-hosted runtimes): Redwood provides audited hosted controls and attestation for customers who don’t want to manage the full stack.
- vs other LLM API providers: emphasize observability (per-token billing traces, audit log exports) and guided cost controls (Optimize recommendations) as security/compliance enablers for governance teams.

Objection handling cheats (short):
- "We need on-site audit access" → offer remote artifact exchange first (SOC 2 report, redacted logs). If still needed, escalate to Legal for controlled on-site engagement with notice and escort.
- "How do you prevent model-data leakage?" → explain isolation, KV/prefix caching limits, no default training use, and provide mitigation: prompt scrubbing, private deployments, and model-variant fallbacks.

Field checklist before putting security slides in a proposal:
- Confirm product plan: Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private.
- Identify whether PHI/PCI/regulated data will be in scope.
- Attach relevant evidence: SOC2, ISO cert, BAA template, pen test summary.
- Determine audit-log retention required and whether export is acceptable.
- Open legal ticket (jira: GTMS-1123) when customer requests unusual audit rights or on-site audits.

Internal TO-DOs / open questions (for GTM & Legal):
- Clarify exact scope of current SOC 2 (services, controls in scope) and maintain a short FAQ page.
- Standardize retention tiers and pricing for longer log retention (730+ days).
- Create scrubbed audit-log sample artifacts and an internal process for redaction.
- Finalize BAA template language and publish in prospect portal.

Example short email snippet for SE to send after a call:
"Thanks for the time today—following up with the docs we discussed: our SOC 2 Type II summary, BAA template for Dedicated/Private, and a sample of the audit-log schema. Let me know what retention window you need and I’ll loop in Legal for next steps."

Appendix: quick model for "what to promise vs what to deliver":
- Promise: "audited controls + configurable retention and BAAs for regulated workloads"
- Deliver: SOC2 report, KMS options, audit-log exports, BAA for Dedicated/Private, architecture diagram, pen test summary.

Notes to self / informal fragments (work-in-progress):
- Should we offer an on-demand SOC2 bridge letter for mid-sales? (talk to compliance: Marco)
- Consider a standard "security one-pager" per plan: hosted/dedicated/private - single sheet with bullets + artifacts links.
- Link to Confluence INF-SEC-3501 for more detailed control mappings.

Document history: drafted by Aisha Patel; reviewed with Marco Chen (security), Lina Rodriguez (legal), Samir Gupta (SE).

----
End of playbook (keep this doc lightweight; move long-form controls map to Confluence).
